title: lightweight-active-probes-and-staged-diagnostic-sampler
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: On noisy alert windows we often lack fast, low-cost evidence to decide whether a pager is actionable. This PR adds a lightweight active-probing framework plus a staged diagnostic sampler that attempts to gather targeted context only when probes indicate degradation. The design minimizes noise, cost, and data retention risk by escalating collection fidelity over time and using the incident-bot's existing permissioned artifact store.

What this provides: 1) active_probes: a configurable set of short-lived probes (HTTP light checks, synthetic DB pings, dependency latency samplers) that run in the incident-bot context and return compact health tuples; 2) staged_sampler: a state machine that transitions from probe-only -> minimal telemetry snapshot (headers, recent error rates, top traces ids) -> full diagnostic bundle (stack traces, span dumps, live query results) only when thresholds are crossed; 3) opt-in runbooks and dry-run mode so teams can validate without automatic artifact retention.

Key constraints and safety: probes run as the incident-bot service account and are rate-limited per-alert and per-oncall; data collected is scrubbed and sampled before upload; a retention TTL is configurable per team; privacy-sensitive artifacts require explicit acceptance from team owners (enforced in the console flow).

Checklist: - [x] core probe runner implementation and config schema - [x] staged sampler state machine and transition rules - [x] small set of probe implementations (http, tcp, pg_ping) - [x] tests for transitions, rate-limits, and scrubbing - [x] docs + console feature flag gating - [x] added metrics and tracing for observability - [x] linear links and migration notes

Testing done: unit + integration harness using local dockerized dependencies; simulated noisy-alert runs (1000 synthetic alerts) to validate rate limiting and collector escalation; manual smoke runs in staging with team opt-in.

How to use: enable feature flag incident_bot.active_probes in console, add a probe_set to the alert rule (examples in docs/active-probes.md), and set sampler.policy to one of (conservative, default, aggressive). Conservative never escalates past minimal snapshot. Default targets 95th percentile latency breach. Aggressive tries full collection on sustained failures.

Related work: builds on previous telemetry-sampler efforts (see ENG-953) and complements the ephemeral-telemetry-digger patterns. This intentionally avoids automatic remediation — it focuses on evidence collection and triage acceleration.
